transcript.text: dyson keeps pulsin on n off like its stutterin, wont stay on proper. batt is full. pls help
AI service unavailable. Please try again in a moment.
it just said service unavailable lol. anyway its a v8 animal, keeps pulsin n cutting out. can u help?

Yep — on a Dyson V8, pulsing/cutting in and out usually means it thinks airflow is blocked, even if the battery is charged.

Try this in order:

1. Empty the bin fully
• Open it and check around the cyclone/shroud area for compacted dust or hair.

2. Check for blockages
• Remove the wand and cleaner head.
• Look through the wand, into the main inlet under the bin/cyclone, and around the brush head.
• Cut/remove hair and thread from the brush bar, especially at both ends.

3. Test it with no attachments
• Turn it on as just the handheld unit.
• If it runs normally: blockage is likely in the wand or floor head.
• If it still pulses: likely filter blockage, internal blockage, or a fault.

4. Wash the filter
• Twist/remove the filter at the back/top of the machine.
• Rinse with cold water only until the water runs clear.
• Shake out water and leave it somewhere warm to dry for at least 24 hours — it must be completely dry before refitting.
• Don’t use detergent, a radiator, tumble dryer, or put it back damp.

5. Try normal mode rather than MAX
• MAX mode can make a weak battery show up more obviously, but it still shouldn’t repeatedly pulse if everything is clear.

If it still pulses with the bin empty, filter fully dry/clean, and no wand or head attached, it’s more likely a battery, motor, or internal airflow sensor issue. On a V8, a tired battery can sometimes show “full” but drop voltage under load. At that point Dyson support or a reputable vacuum repair shop is sensible — avoid opening the battery pack yourself.

A useful quick test: does it pulse only when the floor head is attached, or even as the bare handheld?
yeah still pulses as just the handheld but a bit less. no burning smell or heat or anything tho

If it still pulses as the bare handheld, that rules out the wand and floor head. On a V8 the most common remaining causes are:

1. Dirty/damp filter or a blockage in the cyclone/bin inlet — most likely, since pulsing is Dyson’s usual “airflow restricted” behaviour.
2. Battery voltage dropping under load — possible even if it shows full charge, especially on an older V8.
3. Less commonly, an internal motor/control fault.

Try these checks:

• Remove and wash the filter (the purple/blue filter at the back/top). Cold water only, no soap. Let it dry for a full 24–48 hours before refitting; it must be totally dry.
• With the bin empty, inspect the small opening where dirt enters the cyclone, just above/behind the bin. Hair and fine dust can pack in there.
• Check the holes/mesh around the cyclone for fine dust buildup. A soft dry brush can help — don’t soak the cyclone unit.
• Make sure the bin is properly clicked back into place.

Then test again with the clean, fully dry filter fitted, in normal power mode.

A useful clue is the battery light while it pulses:
• Blue light flashing/pulsing in time with the motor: often blockage/filter/airflow issue.
• Several blue flashes then it stops, especially in MAX mode: battery may be weak.
• No light / unusual red flashing: likely a fault needing repair.

No heat or burning smell is reassuring. But don’t keep repeatedly running it while it’s surging, and don’t use it with a wet filter.

If you clean/dry the filter and clear the inlet but it still pulses with no tools attached, I’d suspect the battery next — V8 batteries commonly lose the ability to supply enough power under load long before they seem completely dead.
the 3 blue lights stay lit the whole time, no red. what should i do next?

Three solid blue lights usually means the battery is supplying power normally — so this points more toward an airflow/filter issue than an obvious battery failure.

Next steps:

1. Wash the filter, even if it looks clean
• Remove the filter at the top/back.
• Rinse under cold water only until water runs clear.
• Shake it thoroughly and leave it to dry for at least 24 hours (48 is safer in a cool/damp house).
• Refit only when completely dry.

2. Check the handheld’s main air path
   With the bin removed/emptied, inspect the opening leading into the cyclone — the airway directly above the bin. Packed fine dust can be hidden there.
• Use a torch/phone light.
• Gently pull out debris with a blunt tool or wooden stick; don’t jab hard into the cyclone.

3. Clean the cyclone shroud
   The perforated metal/plastic section around the cyclone can clog with fine dust. Use a dry soft brush to clear it. Don’t wash the main cyclone assembly unless your specific manual says it is washable.

4. If your V8 has a rear HEPA filter, check that too
   Some V8 variants have a second filter at the back of the machine. Wash it only if it is marked washable, then fully dry it before use.

Don’t test-run it with the filter removed — it can pull dust into the motor.

If it still does the exact same pulse/cut-out after the filter is washed and completely dry, and the internal inlet is clear, the likely next culprit is the battery beginning to fail under load or, less often, the motor/control board. A battery can still show all three blue lights yet sag under load.

At that point, check Dyson’s support site using the serial number (usually behind the battery or on the handle) for troubleshooting/warranty options. If it’s out of warranty, a genuine Dyson replacement battery is generally the least risky first repair; avoid very cheap unbranded packs.

ok washed the filter, its grey not purple lol, never washed it in 3 yrs. water came out black. left it overnight by the radiator n its pulsing way less now but still a bit. the shroud bit was dusty so i wiped it

That’s a strong sign the filter was the main problem — black rinse water after 3 years means it was heavily clogged. If it’s now pulsing less, it may simply still be damp internally or not fully clean yet.

What to do now:

• Take the filter back out and let it dry another 24–48 hours. Overnight often isn’t enough, especially after a deep wash. It needs to be completely dry all the way through, not just dry on the outside.
• Don’t leave it directly on a radiator again — heat can distort or damage the filter material. Leave it in a warm, airy room instead.
• Once fully dry, give it another rinse if the water still comes out grey/dirty, then dry it again fully.

Also:
• Empty the bin and check the air inlet just above it for packed fluff/dust.
• Make sure the bin/cyclone is seated and latched properly.
• A dry brush is ideal for the shroud; avoid getting the cyclone/motor area wet.

Don’t run it without the filter fitted, and don’t keep using it if the filter is even slightly damp.

If it still pulses as a bare handheld after 48 hours of drying and a properly clean filter, then there may be a remaining internal blockage or, less likely, a weakening battery/motor. But the improvement after washing makes the filter/airflow issue the clear first suspect.
emptied the bin already, was rammed full of dog hair, still pulsin a bit tho. anything else i can check?

Yes — but first, let that filter dry properly before doing more test runs. Since it was soaked with black water, it may still be damp inside; that alone can cause continued pulsing. Give it another 24–48 hours in a warm, ventilated room (not directly on the radiator).

While it dries, check these areas:

1. The intake throat where the wand normally clicks in
   Look into the round opening at the front/bottom of the handheld unit. Use your phone torch. Check for a plug of hair/dust just inside.

2. The airway above the bin
   With the bin open/removed, look up into the passage that leads from the intake toward the cyclone. Dog hair can form a felt-like blockage there.

3. Cyclone/shroud holes
   Since the shroud was dusty, use a dry soft brush (old toothbrush/paintbrush) to clear dust from the little holes/mesh. Tap the cyclone gently over a bin.
   Don’t rinse the cyclone/motor body or blast compressed air into it.

4. Bin seal and fitting
   Make sure the clear bin is pushed fully home and the red lever/latch is closed properly. A badly seated bin can mess with airflow.

Then, once the filter is definitely bone dry, test it as the handheld in normal power mode for a minute.

• If the pulsing has stopped or is much better: it was mainly the blocked filter/cyclone, and it may improve further after another proper filter wash/dry.
• If it still pulses identically with a dry clean filter and clear intake: there may be a blockage deeper in the cyclone, or a battery/motor issue. A full battery indication doesn’t completely rule out a tired battery, but the big improvement after cleaning strongly suggests airflow is still the likely culprit.

Also, after three years with pets, make washing the filter roughly monthly (or whenever suction/pulsing starts) part of the routine.
the bin inlet bit was a bit dusty so i wiped it. not sure what else to look at tbh, what about the wand?

Yes, definitely check the wand — dog hair can form a blockage inside it even when it looks fine from one end.

1. Remove the wand from both the handheld and the floor head.
2. Hold it up to a bright light/window and look straight through it. You should see a clear open tube end-to-end.
3. If you can’t see through it, or see a clump:
• Gently push it out using a broom handle, wooden spoon handle, or another long blunt object.
• Don’t use a sharp metal rod that could puncture or crack the tube.
• A flexible bottle brush can help loosen packed fluff.
4. Shake it and tap it gently over a bin; pet hair/dust can be stuck to the inner wall.

Also check the floor head:

• Turn it over and remove hair wrapped around the brush bar, particularly by the end caps.
• Check the short airway where the wand plugs into the head.
• If it has a removable brush bar, take it out and clear both ends/axle area.

However: because yours still pulsed when used without the wand/head, the wand is not the only cause. It could still be partly blocked and make things worse, but the remaining handheld pulsing is most likely the filter not yet fully dry/fully cleared, dusty cyclone shroud, or a restriction further inside the cyclone.

Once the filter has had another 24���48 hours to dry, test in this order:

1. Handheld only, no wand/head.
2. Handheld + wand.
3. Handheld + wand + floor head.

Whichever step brings the pulsing back or makes it worse identifies where the remaining restriction is.
checked the wand n there was a big clump of hair and cat litter stuck at the bottom where the head goes on, pulled it out. its fine now, proper suction n no pulsin

Nice — that’ll have been it. A blockage at the bottom of the wand can make the V8 pulse as it repeatedly loses airflow, and the dirty filter/bin likely made it worse.

Now it’s working:

• Let the filter finish drying fully before using it much, if it isn’t already bone dry.
• Empty the bin before it gets packed full.
• Check the wand and floor-head inlet occasionally, especially with pet hair and litter.
• Wash the filter about once a month, or sooner if suction drops/pulsing returns. Cold water only; dry completely for 24+ hours.

Glad it was a simple fix rather than the battery or motor.
